title: Navigating the Middle Path
content: Like many painters from Eastern Europe who studied in Paris during those golden years of the 1870s,Lajos Deák-Ébnerwanted to apply the achievements of theplein-airtradition without giving up the disciplines of accurate drawing, storytelling, and multi-figure composition.Lajos Deák-Ébner (Hungarian, 1850-1934) Return of the HarvestersThe artist in France who exemplified this middle path wasJules Bastien-Lepage(1848-1884), who was an inspiration to many regionaljuste-milieumovements (the term means 'middle path' or 'happy medium'), not only in Hungary, but also in Spain, England, Scotland, and America.The figures in Deák-Ébner's painting are painted with life and light, and they're developed like characters in a play: a woman with hands on her hips argues with a young man, and a young woman cradles a sheaf of grain in her apron.-----Lajos Deák-Ébneron WikipediaPreviously:Juste-Milieu
